edits.current: THE PRINCIPAL PAYROLL CASILLA ON THE BASE SIDE. The instruction guide defines it as 'los payments gravables (base sujeta a withholding) efectuados a natural persons por concept de salaries, commissions, prestaciones sociales, travel allowances, representation expenses, fees, emolumentos eclesiasticos, compensation received por el trabajo cooperative associate, payments en especie, payments en acciones y, en general, las compensation for personal services'. It is the DEPURATED taxable base of RESIDENT natural persons, not the gross: the ET art. 388 base after non-constitutive income, art. 387 deductions and the 25% exempt income - the base on which the casilla-93 withholding is computed. Non-resident foreign natural persons are NOT in this casilla: their payments are reported in the 'Pagos al exterior' section as sheet-2 rows (casillas 141-146) with the sheet-2 payment concept and country, at the nominal (gross) value, at the 20% rate of ET art. 408 and with no depuration; the employee's tax-residence flag decides the section. Pension income paid by the employer is not in this casilla either: it goes to casilla 78. Note also that the casilla sweeps in fees paid to natural persons under the art. 383 table, which are not employment income - payroll supplies only the employment component. Accumulated by the payment date of each run (payment or credit to account, whichever comes first), not by the pay period the run settles - the same timing rule as casilla 93.

It is the DEPURATED taxable base of RESIDENT natural persons, not the gross: the ET art. 388 base after non-constitutive income, art. 387 deductions and the 25% exempt income - the base on which the casilla-93 withholding is computed. Non-resident foreign natural persons are NOT in this casilla: their payments are reported in the 'Pagos al exterior' section as sheet-2 rows (casillas 141-146) with the sheet-2 payment concept and country, at the nominal (gross) value, at the 20% rate of ET art. 408 and with no depuration; the employee's tax-residence flag decides the section. Pension income paid by the employer is not in this casilla either: it goes to casilla 78. Note also that the casilla sweeps in fees paid to natural persons under the art. 383 table, which are not employment income - payroll supplies only the employment component. Accumulated by the payment date of each run (payment or credit to account, whichever comes first), not by the pay period the run settles - the same timing rule as casilla 93.
